units.translation: The old spelling of this verb is σῴζω [I save] with iota in those forms which have Z, on which see Etym. M. p. 711, 27 σῴζω: τὸ σώζω χωρίς τοῦ ι λέγει ὁ Δίδυμος ἀλλ᾽ ἡ παράδοσις ἔχει τὸ ι — [σῴζω: Didymus says σώζω without the iota, but the tradition has the iota —]. But one must know that whenever it begins from the syllable σω with Z following, it has the iota written adscript, σῴζω σῴζομαι ἔσωζον [I save, I am saved, I was saving], but whenever it is not so, it is not written adscript, as σαώζω σώσω σώσον [I save, I will save, save!]. Similarly other grammarians are cited by L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 7 p. 1703. And thus it is not rarely written in inscriptions, on which see Wecklein in Curis epigraphicis p. 45, and in older manuscripts of writers, though the iota is sometimes also introduced into forms which do not have Z. In M the iota is written adscript in forms which have Z in two places, σῶιζ᾽ [save!] Pr. 374 and σώιζων [saving] Eum. 241, in all the rest it is omitted. The tenses of the verb usual in the tragedians besides the present active and passive are ἔσωζον, ἐσωζόμην, ἔσωσα, σώσω, σέσωσμαι, ἐσώθην [I was saving, I was being saved, I saved, I will save, I have been saved, I was saved]. The ancient form of the perfect σέσωσμαι, which is undoubtedly to be restored everywhere in the scenic poets, is σέσωμαι, on which Photius, σέσωται καὶ σεσωμένος: οἱ παλαιοὶ ἄνευ τοῦ σ, καὶ διεζωμένος φησὶ Θουκυδίδης (1, 6) [σέσωται and σεσωμένος: the ancients without the σ, and Thucydides says διεζωμένος (1, 6)], although copyists have introduced the letter σ into these forms with such consistency that rare examples of the old spelling remain, on which L. Dindorf spoke in Thes. vol. 7 p. 1703 and on Xenoph. Mem. 3, 5, 25 p. 120 ed. Oxon. σέσωται and διασέσωται are preserved in the oldest manuscript of Plato A Critiae p. 109 d. and 110 a. in Cobet Mnem. novae 3 p. 196. It is to be attributed to chance rather than design that the old form σέσωμαι is sometimes found in the writings of later authors, on which it is said in Thes. l. c. where can be added σέσωται from Cyril Alex. vol. 2 p. 426 b. 468 a, while σέσωσται is read there p. 490 b. 497 e. 512 b., and σεσώμεθα p. 524 9.
